title: EPOCHAL – Efficiency, acceptance, and impact of the digitally supported medication process at the transition of care between inpatient and outpatient care, field data collection phase (project phase 1)
summary: Im EPOCHAL Projekt im allgemeinen und auch in der hier vorgestellten Projektphase wird untersucht, wie die Einführung des digital gestützten Medikationsprozesses (dgMP) die arzneimittelbezogenen Aufnahme- und Entlassprozesse im Krankenhaus in Bezug auf die Prozessabläufe, entstehende Aufwände, die Zufriedenheit der Patient:innen und beteiligten Heilberufler:innen in Krankenhaus und angrenzender Versorgung (Ärzt:innen, Apotheker:innen) sowie die Qualität der Arzneimitteldokumentation und Medikationsqualität beeinflusst.
conditions: Efficiency, acceptance, and impact of the digitally supported medication process at the interface between inpatient and outpatient care

interventions.name: The overall objective of the EPOCHAL project (https://innovationsfonds.g-ba.de/projekte/epochal.776) is the evaluation of the so-called “digital gestützter Medikationsprozess” at interfaces of care. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthcare professionals aged 18 or older (hospital-based or private-practice physicians and pharmacists) who, as part of their professional duties, are involved in the medication-related admission and discharge process at the study site
- All adult patients who are capable of giving informed consent, possess sufficient cognitive and language skills to participate in the study, are covered by statutory health insurance, are receiving treatment with five or more medications, are admitted as inpatients at a study site, and have not objected to the installation and use of the ePA following the introduction of the dgMP (opt-out).
- Adult legal representatives (guardians or legal caregivers of individuals incapable of giving consent) whose warded persons are admitted to or discharged from the selected wards at the study sites during the study period
Exclusion criteria:
- individuals with private health insurance (no ePA)
- individuals who have not given their consent
- individuals who are unable to participate due to language or cognitive impairments
